The BA toolkit: where every answer lives

After this lesson you can:
  • Use the repository's documents as a reference system, not a reading list
  • Route any new question to its owning source
  • Keep your knowledge — and this course — verified over time
On this page

  2. Staying current
  3. Where this lives in LoanOS
  4. Knowledge check

1. The routing table

A working BA doesn't memorise; they route. The map:

  • "Is this regulated? By what?" → `docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md` — control families, sources, implementation anchors.
  • "Does the platform do this? How completely?" → `docs/product/complete-system-capability-catalog.md` (status per capability) and `docs/product/product-journey-support-matrix.md` (evidence tier per journey).
  • "What are we building, and what's out of scope?" → `docs/product/what-we-are-building.md`.
  • "How does this subsystem work?" → `docs/architecture/` — origination journey, decision engine design, data governance, digital workers, tenancy.
  • "Why was it decided this way?" → `docs/decisions/` ADRs.
  • "What does this term mean, exactly?" → the course glossary and `docs/gtm/glossary.md`.
  • "How do I operate it?" → the Guide's task articles at `/help/`.

When sources disagree, escalate the discrepancy — the register and design docs win over lessons and marketing, and a disagreement is a documentation bug someone must fix.

2. Staying current

Regulation moves: directions get amended, drafts finalise, commencement dates arrive (the DPDP Rules' phased schedule is a live example).

The platform's answer is verification discipline — the register carries a research baseline date, guides and lessons carry verification dates, and a user-visible change is incomplete until its guidance is updated.

Treat a stale verification date the way an engineer treats a failing test.

This course follows the same rule.

Each lesson shows when it was last verified; if you find drift between a lesson and the register, catalogue or code — the lesson is wrong until proven otherwise.

Fix flows through the curriculum source (`apps/help/academy/content/`), a rebuild, and review.

You are now part of the maintenance loop: welcome to governed lending.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — The regulatory landscape this toolkit keeps you current against.
  • DPDP-RULES-2025 — A live example of phased commencement that demands date-tracking, not assumption.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Document docs/README.md — The documentation map and definition of done.
  • Document docs/product/ba-lending-academy-curriculum.md — This course's own design, contract and governance.
  • Operating guide activate-tenant (open in the Guide) — Where operating knowledge begins when you join a real implementation.
  • App surface /help/ — The Guide & Academy — search, roles, learning paths.

1. A stakeholder asks whether a capability is production-ready. Your first stop?

2. You find a lesson contradicting the regulatory register. What is true?

  1. The lesson — it's newer
  2. The register — and the lesson must be corrected through the curriculum source and rebuilt
  3. Whichever reads better
  4. Neither

B. The register is the maintained source of regulatory truth; course content is downstream and carries a fix-forward duty.
